description: Building web pages that work on every device and every connection: semantic HTML, modern CSS layout, responsive design, media and the JavaScript that brings pages to life. Taught to the depth of a leading front-end web development course.
modelledOn: Duckett, HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites
Duckett, JavaScript and jQuery: Interactive Front-End Web Development
outcomes: Write valid, semantic, accessible HTML documents with correct structure, lists, tables, links, images and forms.
Style pages with CSS selectors, the box model, flexbox and grid, and organise stylesheets maintainably.
Build layouts that adapt to phones, tablets and desktops and remain fast on slow connections.
Embed and control audio, video and canvas content.
Write JavaScript that manipulates the DOM, handles events and validates forms.
Debug and test pages with browser developer tools and publish them to a web host.

units.title: How the Web works and HTML building blocks
topics: Clients, servers, HTTP requests and responses, URLs, browsers and rendering
HTML document structure: doctype, head, body, metadata, character encoding
Elements, attributes, nesting; headings, paragraphs, emphasis, line breaks, comments
Document sections: header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer; why semantics matter
Validation and developer tools; writing a first multi-page site

units.title: Lists and tables
topics: Ordered, unordered and description lists; nested lists for menus
Tables: rows, cells, headers, caption, thead/tbody/tfoot, rowspan and colspan
Accessible tables with scope and headers; when not to use a table
Tabular data from a Ghanaian school timetable or a market price list

units.title: Links and images
topics: Anchors, absolute and relative URLs, fragments, mailto and tel links; link states
Images: formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, WebP), alt text, dimensions, figure and figcaption
Responsive images with srcset and picture; image optimisation for low bandwidth
Icons, favicons and image maps

units.title: Forms
topics: form, input types (text, email, number, date, password, checkbox, radio, file), select, textarea, button
Labels, fieldsets, placeholders and accessibility
HTML5 validation attributes: required, pattern, min, max
GET versus POST and what happens when a form is submitted

units.title: Cascading Style Sheets
topics: Inline, internal and external CSS; selectors (type, class, id, attribute, pseudo-class, pseudo-element); specificity and the cascade
Colour, typography, web fonts, units (px, em, rem, %, vw)
The box model: margin, border, padding, content; box-sizing; display and visibility
Positioning: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky; z-index; floats
Flexbox and CSS grid for page layout; alignment and spacing
Transitions, transforms and simple animations; CSS variables; organising stylesheets

units.title: Responsive HTML
topics: Viewport meta tag; fluid layouts; mobile-first design
Media queries for width, orientation and dark mode
Responsive navigation, images and tables
Performance on 2G/3G: minimising requests, compression, lazy loading; testing with throttling
Accessibility basics: contrast, keyboard navigation, ARIA landmarks

units.title: HTML media
topics: audio and video elements, sources, formats, controls, captions with track
Embedding maps, YouTube and other iframes safely
SVG inline graphics and the canvas element
Considerations for data cost and autoplay

units.title: JavaScript basics
topics: Adding scripts; variables (let, const), types, operators, strings, arrays, objects
Functions, arrow functions, conditionals and loops; the console and debugging
The DOM: selecting elements, changing content and styles, creating and removing nodes
Events: click, input, submit, keyboard; event listeners and the event object
Form validation and dynamic forms; local storage
Fetching JSON from an API and rendering it; introduction to promises
Project: a responsive multi-page site with an interactive feature, published to a static host
